top.title: Tight security as Tinubu visits Jos for APC presidential rally
top.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Security has been beefed up in Jos, the Plateau State capital, ahead of the expected arrival of President Bola Tinubu on Saturday for the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central presidential campaign rally. Our correspondent, who visited several parts of the city, observed a heavy deployment of security personnel at strategic locations, including Hill Station Junction, Zaria Road, Polo Roundabout and parts of Yakubu Gowon Way, as security agencies intensified surveillance ahead of the President’s visit. Tinubu is expected to attend the APC presidential rally scheduled to hold at the Zaria Road Stadium, Jos, where he is also expected to commission three major development projects executed by the Plateau State Government. The projects are the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) Centre in Jos, the Plateau Special Activity Centre (P-SAC) and 50 hybrid Jet Mover buses for inter-local government transportation. Ahead of the President’s visit, Governor Caleb Mutfwang, APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, and former Deputy Governor, Dame Pauline Tallen, inspected the facilities. Speaking on the BPO Centre, Mutfwang described it as a strategic investment in human capital development, job creation and economic empowerment. According to a statement signed by his Director of Press and Public Affairs, Gyang Bere, the governor said the facility, established through a partnership between the Plateau State Government, Outsource Global and MTN Nigeria, has an operational capacity of 800 seats and is projected to generate up to 2,400 direct full-time jobs when fully deployed across three shifts. He said the centre would connect Plateau youths to the global digital economy through customer experience management, technical support and back-office services. Mutfwang added that young people would be able to work for international organisations from Jos and earn in foreign currencies. On the Plateau Special Activity Centre, the governor said the facility was established to strengthen intelligence-driven security operations, stressing that security remained fundamental to sustainable development. The centre comprises a Fusion and Analytical Centre, Geo-Intelligence/GIS Unit, Drone Unit, Training Centre and Profiling Room to enhance intelligence gathering, threat detection, analysis and coordinated security responses. He also said the 50 hybrid buses would improve public transportation, reduce travel costs and enhance connectivity across the state’s 17 local government areas. Meanwhile, during an inspection of the Zaria Road Stadium, venue of the rally, Mutfwang expressed confidence that the event would attract massive participation from APC supporters and stakeholders across the North-Central region. He urged residents to turn out in large numbers to welcome Tinubu, whom he described as a statesman committed to the development and security of Plateau State. The Red Dragons are sorely lacking top quality and depth at present, though, in a position where they have been blessed with talent in years gone by. top.title: The NBA players who appear to have regressed most so far in 2026-27
top.description: Although it's early, we've got enough of a sample size to observe some league-wide trends, such as potential player regressions, which is what we're here to discuss today. Early-season regressions can often be just an illusion, as some players may get off to cold shooting starts, throwing off their games; they could enter a season out of shape and need a month or so to get into game shape before they start looking like their prime selves again; or they could be dealing with undisclosed early-campaign nicks. Regardless, this season, there have been some players who have gotten off to slow starts that have been quite suprising. So let's talk about them. Nikola Jokic (Denver) 2025-26 stats : 27.7 ppg, 12.9 rpg, 10.7 apg, 56.9 FG%, 38.0 3P% 2026-27 stats : 23.5 ppg, 10.8 rpg, 9.0 apg, 50.0 FG%, 23.3 3P% It almost feels asinine to discuss Nikola Jokic in a negative light, as he remains an All-NBA-level performer and an extremely impactful player, one who makes his team 9.7 points per 100 possessions better and who ranks Top 5 in VORP and BPM. However, Jokic hasn't been at his usual otherworldly self this season; it's the first time in four years that he doesn't lead the league in both of the aforementioned advanced metrics, while his Denver Nuggets are just 6-4 through 10 games and look like a Play-In-caliber team, at least as things stand now. That's all to say: Jokic remains a top-level player, but he hasn't played like the franchise-carrying supernova that he's been since 2020-21. Could this be a sign of age and his lack of elite fitness starting to catch up to him? Or is it simply a slow start for the Serbian superstar, one in part caused by his three-point shot being ice-cold at the moment? We're starting to think it could be a bit of the latter, as over his past five games, Jokic's numbers are starting to look more Jokic-like at 25.8 points, 11.8 rebounds, 8.8 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.0 blocks per game. Joel Embiid (Philadelphia) 2025-26 stats : 26.9 ppg, 7.7 rpg, 3.9 apg, 48.9 FG%, 33.3 3P% 2026-27 stats : 17.9 ppg, 8.8 rpg, 3.7 apg, 37.4 FG%, 11.1 3P% It's somewhat ironic that the two players who brought the center position back to the forefront are the first two players we discuss here, but we couldn't mention Jokic and not bring up his former rival in so many MVP races, Joel Embiid , as a player who has also regressed mightily this season. Injuries have held Embiid to 39, 19 and 38 games over the past three seasons, respectively, and it's entirely possible that those constant health issues have made it so we'll never see a prime Embiid again. If that is the case, that would be unfortunate for NBA fans, as the big man was absolutely dominant in his prime, a 7-footer who could shoot, drive, post-up, create for teammates and block shots on the other end of the floor, as well as gobble up rebounds. Embiid's statistical regression could be a matter of usage, too, as the former Kansas standout has a career-low 28.4 percent usage rate in 2026-27.

top.title: Proof: Real Madrid enjoy huge advantage over Barcelona in La Liga foul statistics
top.description: Proof: Real Madrid enjoy huge advantage over Barcelona in La Liga foul statistics Barcelona and Real Madrid are experiencing contrasting treatment in La Liga’s foul statistics, with Hansi Flick’s side committing more fouls while receiving considerably fewer free-kicks than their biggest rivals. The numbers, covering the opening 12 league matches of the 2026-27 season and highlighted by Mundo Deportivo , show an intriguing difference between the two title contenders. As such, Barcelona have committed 130 fouls and received 122, producing a negative differential of eight. Real Madrid, meanwhile, have committed just 102 fouls while winning 171, giving them a remarkable positive differential of 69. The contrast raises questions about how the two teams are experiencing refereeing decisions, especially at a time when Los Blancos continuously campaign against refereeing standards in the league. Real Madrid enjoy significant advantage over Barcelona Barcelona are the second least-fouled team in La Liga, behind only Real Sociedad, who have received 113 free-kicks. Barcelona ahve conceded the second-fewest number of fouls in La Liga this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Despite dominating possession and frequently attempting to progress through opposition pressure, the Catalans have not received the same number of referee decisions in their favour as Real Madrid. As for Los Blancos, Mourinho’s team occupy the opposite end of the comparison. Their 171 fouls received are the highest in the division, while their 102 committed are the fewest. Furthermore, the individual statistics reinforce the contrast, as Fermin Lopez has committed 16 fouls, while Lamine Yamal, who has won 20 fouls, and Xavi Espart have registered 13 each. Conversely, Jude Bellingham leads the league for fouls won with 31. Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr. have 23 apiece, while Arda Guler has drawn 21. The El Clasico example Cucurella was never penalised for his challenges on Lamine Yamal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The October 25 meeting at Spotify Camp Nou, which Barcelona lost 1-2, offered a particularly relevant illustration. Marc Cucurella repeatedly challenged Lamine Yamal, with several incidents generating frustration among Barcelona fans. Several supporters highlighted the defender’s aggressive approach towards the young winger, while football pundits also questioned the decision not to award a free-kick when Yamal went down under Cucurella’s pressure late in the match. Now, there will be a debate regarding the matter, but the aforementioned statistics certainly bring forward a key question: if Real Madrid are indeed winning more fouls than any other team, why do they criticise La Liga officials? More importantly, is their campaign against referees influencing these statistics? If so, where is the transparency?

top.description: SPRINGFIELD — Hardware was handed out to some teams, while others shed tears. It was the district championship for high school football in Missouri on Friday, Nov. 14. The playoffs continue to be wild, with upsets and crazy finishes. Here’s everything that happened to Springfield area teams in the district title game. Nixa hangs on to defeat red-hot Ozark There isn’t a single team in the area that has improved more as the season went along than Ozark (6-6). Nixa felt Ozark’s wrath throughout the district championship game. The Eagles had to hold on to a 34-27 win to secure the title. Nixa (10-2) coach John Perry took to social media , calling Ozark’s performance the best he’d seen in seven years. Ozark had the ball at Nixa’s 10-yard line with less than 10 seconds to play. Down a touchdown, Ozark tried to fire pass after pass to the end zone from quarterback Caden O’Donnell. Fair Grove football: Eagles turn whiteboard motivation into district championship reality Nixa used its own starting quarterback, Adam McKnight, to play defensive end. McKnight went around the edge and sacked O’Donnell to end the game. Nixa’s big-play ability was too much for Ozark. Nixa trailed 14-13 at halftime with its back against the wall. McKnight threw two of his three touchdown passes in the first half. He found Carter Mabe from 35 yards and Austin White from 60. Ozark countered with a 1-yard rushing score from Jett Easley. top.title: Clough's longevity: landmark achievement or indictment on football?
top.description: Nigel Clough took charge of Mansfield Town in November 2020 [Shutterstock] Becoming the longest-serving manager at a club takes some doing in the fickle world of football. Sticking around at two clubs long enough to hold that mantle is just about unprecedented. But Mansfield Town's Nigel Clough is about to redefine longevity as a manager when it comes to working at sides that make up the top 92 in the English pyramid. "I don't think it's particularly an achievement; I think it's more an indictment of football that nobody else has lasted that long," Clough told BBC Sport. This weekend he becomes the longest-serving manager – in terms of active years in the job and league matches at the helm – of the Stags, where he surpasses club great Ian Greaves. The 16 years Clough spent at Burton Albion, which took in around 900 matches across two spells spanning more than two decades, means the record at the east Staffordshire side is already his. Former England forward Clough is now six years and one week into the Stags job and is the second longest-serving manager across England's top four leagues - behind only Mikel Arteta at Arsenal - but he does not see his staying power as anything special. "I don't really think about it that much, I have to say. I'm just trying to get through the week," said Clough, who has been in charge of Mansfield for 329 matches across all competitions. When time pays dividends While Clough's players, as well as Mansfield fans have a different take on what his lengthy tenure at the One Call Stadium has meant, the 60-year-old reeled off the names of legendary past managers - his late father and iconic Nottingham Forest boss Brian Clough included - when reflecting on what joy clubs would have by sticking by their manager. "When you look back 20 or 30 years, my dad was at Forest for 18 years, Alex Ferguson was at Manchester United for so long and then there was Arsene Wenger at Arsenal. That was at the top level, but even lower down there was a lot of managers who stayed a lot of years," he said "I just think it's sad the way football is going at the moment. The first bad period that people have, a month, two months or something like that, and the manager is the one that goes." Clough, who played in the top flight for Forest, Liverpool and Manchester City, has been in management for 28 years and been in charge of just four clubs - Mansfield, Burton, Derby County and Sheffield United - in that time. Since bounding from non-league level - where he spent the first 10 years of his management career in his first spell at Burton - to take the reins of Derby in the Championship in 2009, no-one has overseen more matches than Clough's 893 across England's top four divisions. The latest statistics from the League Managers' Association show that managers across those leagues are now staying in their jobs for less than a year on average. top.description: Negreira case investigation effectively closed as Real Madrid await crucial Barcelona financial documents The Negreira case remains one of the biggest controversies rocking Spanish football at the moment. Real Madrid continue to push for answers over Barcelona’s financial relationship with the former vice-president of the Spanish refereeing committee. Now, according to Que T’hi Jugues , the judicial committee has officially concluded its witness hearings. Only certain financial documents from Barcelona remain outstanding before a decision can be made on whether the case proceeds to trial. Former Barcelona officials defend usefulness of referee reports Former Barcelona B manager Gerard Lopez and ex-delegate Toni Alonso were the final witnesses to testify before investigating judge Alejandra Gil on Friday. Both defended the usefulness of the refereeing reports prepared by Javier Enriquez, son of former refereeing official Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira. Lopez coached Barcelona’s reserves between 2015 and 2018 and explained how reports on refereeing tendencies helped, especially in the lower divisions. Luis Enrique denied knowing of the technical reports that are at the centre of the Negreira case. (Photo by JAVIER SORIANO / AFP) (Photo by JAVIER SORIANO/AFP via Getty Images) Their testimony, however, contrasts with that of former first-team managers such as Luis Enrique and Ernesto Valverde. The two managers claimed that they were unaware of the reports or had never used them in any capacity during their time at the club. Barcelona continue to maintain that the payments were exclusively for technical consultancy services and not an attempt to influence refereeing decisions. Real Madrid await final documents before crucial judicial decision Real Madrid had requested a six-month extension to the investigation, alongside the prosecution, but the judge rejected the request in September. Nevertheless, Los Blancos successfully secured a partial ruling from the Barcelona Provincial Court requiring Barcelona to submit financial audits and reports covering 2010 to 2021. These are the documents still outstanding from the Catalan club before the investigation officially concludes. Real Madrid are closely following the proceedings of the Negreira case. (Photo by Dan Mullan/Getty Images) Once the documents are received, Judge Gil is expected to decide, potentially in early 2027, whether to dismiss the proceedings or send the case to trial. The investigation concerns payments reportedly totalling €8.4 million over 17 years to Negreira and related companies. Real Madrid are closely following the proceedings because, should Barcelona be found guilty, no other club would have been more affected than them. It remains to be seen how Judge Gil assesses the findings of this investigation and whether the case goes to trial in 2027.

top.title: “She’s so good on the ball”: Eva Olid lavishes praise on surprise player ahead of Crystal Palace match
top.description: “She’s so good on the ball”: Eva Olid lavishes praise on surprise player ahead of Crystal Palace match Manchester United Women manager Eva Olid has been speaking to the media ahead of her side’s home match in the Women’s Super League (WSL) against Crystal Palace. Squad updates Olid admitted she was still waiting for physio reports, but the only player definitely out is Scarlett Hill , who will be out of action for weeks. Hanna Lundkvist form The Catalan coach praised her side’s tactical performance versus Aston Villa last weekend and singled out the Swedish international Lundkvist for special praise. Olid explained, “I think she’s a player who can play in different positions. She can play as a full-back, a wing-back or a wide centre-back. With the national team, she’s also playing as a number six.” She continued, “she’s so good on the ball. She’s a player who can come inside and can play out wide. As a manager, you always like having those kinds of players because you know they’re versatile and can play in different positions, giving different things to the team.” Crystal Palace threat Explaining the type of threat Palace will pose, she asserted, “I expect a very competitive match. They’ve been having good matches, especially their last result against Tottenham on Wednesday. It was a very competitive match, and they could have won the game.” Olid continued, “for that reason, I expect a really good match, tactically and in terms of intensity. I hope everyone enjoys it.” Despite her side being on an 11-game unbeaten streak, Olid still wanted to focus on what her side needs to work on. She added, “I know it’s repetitive, but we’re still in a process. We know there are a lot of things we have to improve. For me, it’s so important that I can see the team gaining a lot of confidence on the ball and starting to connect with each other. That’s what we need. For me, that’s a big step from where we started the season to where we are now, particularly in terms of confidence on the ball and connections between the players.” Finally, she also warned her players that the longer their streak goes on, the harder it will be to maintain. She explained, “I think all teams are motivated when they play against Manchester United in general. But if they know that we haven’t lost in 11 games, I think that’s going to give the opposition even more motivation. We just have to stay focused and take it week by week. We need to try to win the next match independently of everything else. Just the next match and nothing more.” United will kick off later today at 12:45 at the Progress with Unity Stadium. online polls Featured image by Ben Roberts Photo via Getty Images

top.title: Suns Announcer Mocks Devin Booker Trade Idea With 4-Word Quip
top.description: Devon Booker of the Suns © X/@Suns Amid the Phoenix Suns’ struggles this season, Devin Booker has resurfaced in trade rumors. On Friday, Eric Pincus of Bleacher Report floated the idea of Phoenix sending Booker to the Atlanta Hawks in exchange for CJ McCollum, Dorian Finney-Smith, Corey Kispert, rookie Kingston Flemings, and a protected 2028 first-round pick. Suns color analyst Eddie Johnson wasn’t feeling this idea, however. The 17-year NBA veteran mocked Pincus’ proposed trade with a four-word retort. “Put down the (tequila)!” Johnson tweeted on Friday. — Eddie A Johnson (@Jumpshot8) November 13, 2026 Though Booker continues to shoot efficiently in his 12th NBA campaign, his 25.5 points per game is his lowest scoring average in the past seven seasons. Still, the five-time NBA All-Star is a solid playmaker, putting up 5.0 assists per game while cutting down his turnovers to 2.5 a night. Booker is far and away the Suns’ best offensive weapon, but his individual numbers haven’t translated into team success early in the season. Holding the 11th spot in the Western Conference with their 5-6 record, the Suns got off to a 1-5 start before bouncing back with four wins over the past eight days. On offense, the Suns have been middling, ranking 15th with an offensive rating of 113.8. Phoenix has fared even worse on the other end of the floor, as their bottom-5 defense has allowed opponents to shoot 46.5% from the field and 37.4% from deep. Phoenix has plenty of areas to fix, but in Johnson’s eyes (a Suns forward in the late 80s), trading Booker isn’t a viable solution. Report: Suns Intend to “Build Around” Devin Booker Amid Rumors of Players’ Frustration With Lack of Point Guard In late October, insider Chris Haynes reported “growing frustration” among Suns players over the lack of a true point guard on their roster. While Booker doesn’t exactly fit that mold, the Suns are apparently committed to him as their centerpiece. Appearing on SiriusXM NBA Radio this past Wednesday, insider Mike Scotto said that Booker remains the face of the franchise. “From every indication I’ve gotten, the Phoenix Suns want to keep Devin Booker, and they want to continue to build around him…And, for Devin Booker, every indication I’ve gotten is he still wants to be a Sun for life.” As for finding a court general to relieve Booker of playmaking duties, there happens to be a former All-Star guard with his eyes on the Valley. On Friday, Sam Amick reported that the New Orleans Pelicans’ Dejounte Murray has “strong interest” in joining the Suns , though the Pelicans and the Suns reportedly have not engaged in talks yet. top.title: Barcelona secure HUGE €300m financial boost to transform Camp Nou
top.description: FC Barcelona v Getafe CF - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona have secured a massive €300 million financial injection to continue the transformation of their iconic stadium. The Catalan club finalised a new bond issue to guarantee the completion of the Camp Nou refurbishment, ensuring the ground becomes Europe's largest. Huge financial boost secured Barca have successfully finalised a massive €300 million bond issue to fund their ambitious stadium project. The latest financial manoeuvre is designed specifically for use on the completion of the ongoing refurbishment of the Camp Nou . The transaction received the official green light from the National Securities Market Commission (CNMV) prior to being announced. This crucial regulatory approval allows the Catalan side to push forward with their infrastructure plans without delay. Strategic global financial partnership In order to facilitate this massive financial undertaking, Barcelona partnered with industry giants to secure the necessary funding. Goldman Sachs acted as the sole placement agent for the complex transaction. This strategic move highlights the scale of the investment required to finalise the stadium overhaul. The €300m injection will enable continued, uninterrupted progress on transforming the Camp Nou into a thoroughly modern arena. Building Europe's largest stadium The Camp Nou project remains the absolute centrepiece of the wider Espai Barca development. The club have made it clear that this specific funding is essential to bringing their ultimate vision for the surrounding infrastructure to life. Once the extensive refurbishment is fully complete, the ground will officially become the largest capacity football stadium in Europe. This record-breaking size is a major aspect of the club's long-term operational strategy. Focus on premium hospitality Looking ahead, the newly injected funds will allow developers to finalise the specific interior offerings of the new stadium. A major focus of the transformed Camp Nou will be an extensive offer of premium and hospitality spaces. These high-end additions are expected to completely modernise the matchday experience for supporters visiting the arena. The completion of these crucial phases remains the immediate priority for the club following the successful €300m bond issue.

top.description: Davenport's Zayden Garza runs the ball while Somerset's Michael Gonzalez prepares for a tackle during the Class 4A Division I first-round playoff game at Heroes Stadium in San Antonio, Texas on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. Davenport defeated Somerset 35-32. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Davenport running back Zayden Garza had three prescient words written on his nose strip. "Against all odds." Behind Garza's three fourth-quarter touchdowns, Davenport overcame the odds as the Wolves rallied to beat Somerset 35-32 in a Class 4A Division I first-round playoff game Friday at Heroes Stadium. Garza rushed for 245 yards on 35 carries, leading a Davenport rushing attack that gashed Somerset for 309 yards and rumbled back from a 24-14 deficit. The Wolves advanced to the second round to play Corpus Christi Miller next week. Miller trounced Zapata 52-0 in their bi-district playoff clash on Friday. "I definitely knew I was going to come here and do what I do, no matter what," Garza said. "One out of three people had us losing this game. They're (Somerset) the number one seed, we came in as the fourth seed, dropped some games, but we're here to show that it doesn't matter. We got in and we're going to make a run." Somerset (8-3) came in as District 14-4A-I champions, but the Bulldogs had lost to Davenport (8-3) each of the previous two seasons when they competed in the same district. The Wolves suffered close losses to Kerrville Tivy and Fredericksburg in their new home, 13-4A-I. Garza said Davenport was able to wear down Somerset with its grinding rushing attack late in the game. "They (Somerset) had some guys that played both ways and they were going to load the box on us," Garza said. "We knew those guys were going to get tired once that fourth quarter comes along and they weren't going to be able hang with our tempo. nigeria.title: Tight security as Tinubu visits Jos for APC presidential rally
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Security has been beefed up in Jos, the Plateau State capital, ahead of the expected arrival of President Bola Tinubu on Saturday for the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central presidential campaign rally. Our correspondent, who visited several parts of the city, observed a heavy deployment of security personnel at strategic locations, including Hill Station Junction, Zaria Road, Polo Roundabout and parts of Yakubu Gowon Way, as security agencies intensified surveillance ahead of the President’s visit. Tinubu is expected to attend the APC presidential rally scheduled to hold at the Zaria Road Stadium, Jos, where he is also expected to commission three major development projects executed by the Plateau State Government. The projects are the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) Centre in Jos, the Plateau Special Activity Centre (P-SAC) and 50 hybrid Jet Mover buses for inter-local government transportation. Ahead of the President’s visit, Governor Caleb Mutfwang, APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, and former Deputy Governor, Dame Pauline Tallen, inspected the facilities. Speaking on the BPO Centre, Mutfwang described it as a strategic investment in human capital development, job creation and economic empowerment. According to a statement signed by his Director of Press and Public Affairs, Gyang Bere, the governor said the facility, established through a partnership between the Plateau State Government, Outsource Global and MTN Nigeria, has an operational capacity of 800 seats and is projected to generate up to 2,400 direct full-time jobs when fully deployed across three shifts. He said the centre would connect Plateau youths to the global digital economy through customer experience management, technical support and back-office services. Mutfwang added that young people would be able to work for international organisations from Jos and earn in foreign currencies. On the Plateau Special Activity Centre, the governor said the facility was established to strengthen intelligence-driven security operations, stressing that security remained fundamental to sustainable development. The centre comprises a Fusion and Analytical Centre, Geo-Intelligence/GIS Unit, Drone Unit, Training Centre and Profiling Room to enhance intelligence gathering, threat detection, analysis and coordinated security responses. He also said the 50 hybrid buses would improve public transportation, reduce travel costs and enhance connectivity across the state’s 17 local government areas. Meanwhile, during an inspection of the Zaria Road Stadium, venue of the rally, Mutfwang expressed confidence that the event would attract massive participation from APC supporters and stakeholders across the North-Central region. He urged residents to turn out in large numbers to welcome Tinubu, whom he described as a statesman committed to the development and security of Plateau State. nigeria.title: Argentina beaten by Uruguay in first game since Messi retirement
nigeria.description: Argentina suffered a 2-1 defeat against Uruguay on Friday in their first game since Lionel Messi’s retirement from international football. A second-half own goal by Argentina defender Leonardo Balerdi followed by a fluky effort from Uruguay midfielder Maxi Araujo sealed defeat for the 2026 World Cup runners-up. Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alavarez gave Argentina hope of a comeback with a 73rd-minute strike but Uruguay held on to clinch a third victory for new manager Diego Forlan. Messi played his final game for Argentina in an emotional farewell friendly victory over Benin last month, calling time on a glittering career that spanned 207 caps and 125 goals. With the 39-year-old genius missing, Argentina struggled to break down a resilient Uruguay team for long stretches of Friday’s friendly. Nico Paz had Argentina’s best chance of the first half, but saw his shot well-saved by Uruguay goalkeeper Cristopher Fiermarin. Uruguay made the breakthrough soon after half-time when a Giorgian de Arrascaeta free-kick from the left caused chaos in the Argentina defence. Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez attempted to clear with a header but his effort instead cannoned off team-mate Balerdi and into the net. De Arrascaeta then set up Uruguay’s second in the 53rd minute, his corner appearing to hit Araujo’s shoulder before looping high into the net. nigeria.title: Hundreds of million for 90 minutes, peanuts for a lifetime of service, by Stephanie Shaakaa
nigeria.description: *Nigeria’s Broken Scale of Value When the Super Falcons clinched their record-extending tenth Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in July 2025, the Presidency rolled out the red carpet. The players received national honours, three-bedroom apartments in Abuja and the promise of the naira equivalent of $100,000 each. The financial rewards were eventually fulfilled in November 2026. Barely had that celebration settled when another Nigerian women’s team made history. The Flamingos conquered the world, becoming the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Once again, the presidential purse swung open: ₦100 million for each player, secured in savings certificates because of their young age, ₦100 million in cash for the coach and ₦50 million for each member of the technical crew. The Senate also announced a separate ₦100 million reward. Let us be clear: nobody begrudges these young girls their glory. They trained hard, carried the green-and-white flag with pride and earned their moment in the sun. Their achievement deserves recognition, and the decision to preserve their rewards in savings instruments rather than hand enormous sums directly to teenagers is commendable. The problem is not that the government rewards sporting excellence. It is what the speed, scale and enthusiasm of these announcements reveal about the Nigerian state’s priorities. There is a disturbing arithmetic to our national life: hundreds of millions for 90 minutes of football, and peanuts, sometimes outright silence, for a lifetime of service. See the contrast in Abuja. When a trophy arrives at the Presidential Villa, the government can announce substantial financial commitments, organise receptions and put together carefully structured reward packages. Even the decision to protect the Flamingos’ money through savings certificates demonstrates an ability to think ahead and make financial arrangements in the interest of young beneficiaries. Yet, outside the celebratory atmosphere of the Villa, citizens encounter a different government, one that appears to require endless negotiations, industrial threats and public agitation before certain obligations receive the attention they deserve. The contrast extends beyond workers and pensioners. Consider the survivors of the Yelewata massacre in Benue State. Having lost family members, homes and livelihoods to violence, many displaced residents continue to struggle with food, healthcare, decent shelter and other basic necessities. Investigations into conditions in Benue’s displacement camps have documented irregular food distribution, inadequate sanitation, poor healthcare facilities and families struggling to secure even one proper meal a day. These are Nigerians whose lives have been shattered by violence. They are not asking for presidential honours or millions in savings certificates. nigeria.title: Do you think your woman is having an affair?
nigeria.description: By Bunmi Sofola Here, a marriage counselor who has spent 16 years sifting through the ruins of other people’s relationships, gives his analysis of how a partnership can lose its way, and a few suggestions for not letting it happen. (a) Signs she is having an affair Look for a sudden short-term drop-off sex: Everyone has appetites – exactly where is she satisfying hers? Radically different sexual behavior: If she suddenly starts suggesting things he hasn’t done before, or doing things every differently even if it’s better, where is she getting the ideas from? Sudden increase in working hours: This can easily be innocent, but where’s the extra cash? (You might never know if lover boy is giving her over-time pay!) Sexually transmitted infections: Towels and toilet seat explanations simply aren’t good enough. (b) Things she is getting from an affair that she is not getting at home Excitement that is the main thing. Having a secret life. If you are clever enough, your marriage should be her secret life! (c) Full time attention He is trying harder than you. Usually a stop up, someone better than the husband in at least one respect – looks, money, youth. (d) Mistakes husbands make Not adjusting to the fact that you are married. Like it or not, you are now part of a double act, and you can’t carry on as if nothing’s happened. Women like to see visible signs of commitment, so cut down on after work drinks with the boys. (e) Getting Fat It sounds harsh, but there are a lot of thin guys out there who’ll be trying if on your wife. (f) Taking her for granted Undervaluing her, expecting her to be there and expecting her not to get suspicious when you’re having affairs. (f) Over-working A lot of high-achieving guys drive themselves hard often thinking it is for sake of their wives or family. But putting in excessive hours to generate your wealth just provides her with motive, means and opportunity for adultery. However, painful, there comes a time when a marriage is beyond repair, continues the counselor. According to him, Violence is not a good sign”. nigeria.title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China – White House
nigeria.description: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday. Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said. The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said. One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said. “I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call. Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. “China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added. Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said. Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year. But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin. Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said. “The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said. The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal. “We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration… and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said. Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen. Read Also: 6,000 Flight Cancelled: US air travel resumption will ‘take time’ A conference starting Monday at the United Nations in Geneva will discuss how to establish curbs and prohibitions on such weapons, called killer robots by some. But some analysts doubt the discussions at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) will keep pace with the fast-changing weapons. AFP looks at three key questions ahead of the conference. What are LAWS? Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) “can identify, select, and engage a target without the intervention of a human operator in the execution of these tasks,” said Jean-Marc Rickli, head of global and emerging risks at the Geneva Centre for Security Policy. Autonomous weapons have long existed. An anti-personnel mine “is an autonomous weapon in the sense that it explodes when someone steps on it,” said Laure de Roucy-Rochegonde of the Centre for Geopolitics of Technology at the French Institute of International Relations (IFRI). But with the proliferation of AI-enhanced drones, such weapons are now “capable of selecting and engaging a target that was not predetermined, adapting to their environment without human intervention,” said Rickli. So the critical issue for potential regulators lies in determining the level of human control over the decision to employ such a weapon. The United States refers to an “appropriate levels of human judgement” in the use of autonomous weapons. France maintains that a human must remain in the decision-making loop and bans “lethal autonomous weapons systems” (LAWS) but permits “partially autonomous” systems known as PLAWS. “The human role is always ensured through what is termed ‘appropriate control’ by a military commander — a concept that varies in scope depending on the system’s criticality and the operational context,” said Rear Admiral Vincent Sebastien, deputy director of the French defence ministry’s Agency for Defence Artificial Intelligence (AMIAD). The ethical issues? “We are now dangerously close to crossing a moral red line: the autonomous targeting of humans by machines,” UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, and International Committee of the Red Cross president Mirjana Spoljaric warned in a joint statement in August. nigeria.description: Flights in the United States were resuming on Saturday after being grounded for several hours due to a major communications outage, though authorities said returning to normal operations would take time. The nationwide stop on Friday sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events. The incident marked only the second time such an alert had been issued in US airspace — which is among the busiest in the world — since the 9/11 attacks. The ground stop lasted around four hours and was lifted at 8:15 pm Eastern Time (0115 GMT Saturday). Federal Aviation Administration officials reopened the airspace on Friday night “after restoring full functionality” at air traffic control facilities, according to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy. “It will take us time (to) resume normal operations… Our top priority is the safety of you and your family when you fly,” Duffy said. Administration officials blamed the incident on telecommunications issues with decades-old equipment, adding there was no evidence of foul play. “This is a legacy system problem,” Duffy said. “We have old, old switches, old routers. “We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down, and went down everywhere. It got overloaded.” Duffy had formally asked Congress on Thursday for $30.1 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the air traffic control System. As the ground stop was lifted, he repeated his plea. “I’m going to say it a million times: the Congress has to give the resources to the president so he can finish this bill,” he said. 6,000 flights canceled There were almost 6,000 flights canceled, including some international routes, according to FlightAware, a tracking platform. Footage from airports around the country showed gates full, with planes waiting on taxiways. Passengers thronged concourses, desperate for information about an outage that had thrown their plans into chaos. “We’re trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too,” said Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California. entertainment.title: FWIFT 2026 Convention Communique: Industry Leaders Charge Women in Media to Embrace Cross-Border Growth
entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media. There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. Consequently, the manager was expected to take charge of the establishment without the necessary authority and cooperation from everyone involved. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. entertainment.title: Celebrating 50 Years of Nourishment: Maltina Introduces Its New Look to Trade Partners
entertainment.description: Maltina has unveiled its refreshed visual identity at a trade launch event in Lagos, marking 50 years of nourishing Nigerian homes and introducing a new look for the iconic malt brand while retaining the taste and nutritional qualities consumers have come to love. Held on Friday, November 6, 2026, at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Ikeja, the event brought together business partners, distributors, consumers and other distinguished guests to celebrate the milestone and experience the refreshed brand through interactive activities, entertainment and product showcases. First introduced as Maltona in 1976 and renamed Maltina in 1977, the brand has maintained a strong presence in Nigerian homes for over five decades. Its journey has been defined by a commitment to nourishment, including its introduction of multivitamin enrichment in 1993 and calcium fortification in 2009. Beyond its product innovations, Maltina continues to build meaningful connections with consumers through initiatives such as Maltina Nourishment Tour, Maltina Dance All, Maltina Teacher of the Year (MTOTY), and its Christmas and Ramadan festive campaigns, creating opportunities for learning, participation and shared experiences. Speaking at the event, Sarah Agha , Marketing Director, Nigerian Breweries Plc., reflected on the brand’s journey and the thinking behind its refreshed identity. She highlighted Maltina’s longstanding commitment to nourishment and happiness, noting that the new look represents a more contemporary and confident expression of the brand as it prepares for its next chapter. The refreshed packaging features an enriched signature orange, gold accents and barley elements that reinforce Maltina’s malt credentials. The updated sunrays represent vitality and optimism, while the more prominent calcium coin highlights its nourishment proposition. The gold crown cork and the addition of ‘Since 1976’ further celebrate the brand’s heritage. She reassured consumers that while the brand’s visual identity has evolved, its familiar taste and nutritional credentials remain unchanged. She said “This is not just about refreshing our identity; it is about reaffirming our commitment to nourishment and to families across Nigeria. Our new look makes these commitments even more visible. sports.title: The NBA players who appear to have regressed most so far in 2026-27
sports.description: Although it's early, we've got enough of a sample size to observe some league-wide trends, such as potential player regressions, which is what we're here to discuss today. Early-season regressions can often be just an illusion, as some players may get off to cold shooting starts, throwing off their games; they could enter a season out of shape and need a month or so to get into game shape before they start looking like their prime selves again; or they could be dealing with undisclosed early-campaign nicks. Regardless, this season, there have been some players who have gotten off to slow starts that have been quite suprising. So let's talk about them. Nikola Jokic (Denver) 2025-26 stats : 27.7 ppg, 12.9 rpg, 10.7 apg, 56.9 FG%, 38.0 3P% 2026-27 stats : 23.5 ppg, 10.8 rpg, 9.0 apg, 50.0 FG%, 23.3 3P% It almost feels asinine to discuss Nikola Jokic in a negative light, as he remains an All-NBA-level performer and an extremely impactful player, one who makes his team 9.7 points per 100 possessions better and who ranks Top 5 in VORP and BPM. However, Jokic hasn't been at his usual otherworldly self this season; it's the first time in four years that he doesn't lead the league in both of the aforementioned advanced metrics, while his Denver Nuggets are just 6-4 through 10 games and look like a Play-In-caliber team, at least as things stand now. That's all to say: Jokic remains a top-level player, but he hasn't played like the franchise-carrying supernova that he's been since 2020-21. Could this be a sign of age and his lack of elite fitness starting to catch up to him? Or is it simply a slow start for the Serbian superstar, one in part caused by his three-point shot being ice-cold at the moment? We're starting to think it could be a bit of the latter, as over his past five games, Jokic's numbers are starting to look more Jokic-like at 25.8 points, 11.8 rebounds, 8.8 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.0 blocks per game. Joel Embiid (Philadelphia) 2025-26 stats : 26.9 ppg, 7.7 rpg, 3.9 apg, 48.9 FG%, 33.3 3P% 2026-27 stats : 17.9 ppg, 8.8 rpg, 3.7 apg, 37.4 FG%, 11.1 3P% It's somewhat ironic that the two players who brought the center position back to the forefront are the first two players we discuss here, but we couldn't mention Jokic and not bring up his former rival in so many MVP races, Joel Embiid , as a player who has also regressed mightily this season. Injuries have held Embiid to 39, 19 and 38 games over the past three seasons, respectively, and it's entirely possible that those constant health issues have made it so we'll never see a prime Embiid again. If that is the case, that would be unfortunate for NBA fans, as the big man was absolutely dominant in his prime, a 7-footer who could shoot, drive, post-up, create for teammates and block shots on the other end of the floor, as well as gobble up rebounds. Embiid's statistical regression could be a matter of usage, too, as the former Kansas standout has a career-low 28.4 percent usage rate in 2026-27.

sports.title: Proof: Real Madrid enjoy huge advantage over Barcelona in La Liga foul statistics
sports.description: Proof: Real Madrid enjoy huge advantage over Barcelona in La Liga foul statistics Barcelona and Real Madrid are experiencing contrasting treatment in La Liga’s foul statistics, with Hansi Flick’s side committing more fouls while receiving considerably fewer free-kicks than their biggest rivals. The numbers, covering the opening 12 league matches of the 2026-27 season and highlighted by Mundo Deportivo , show an intriguing difference between the two title contenders. As such, Barcelona have committed 130 fouls and received 122, producing a negative differential of eight. Real Madrid, meanwhile, have committed just 102 fouls while winning 171, giving them a remarkable positive differential of 69. The contrast raises questions about how the two teams are experiencing refereeing decisions, especially at a time when Los Blancos continuously campaign against refereeing standards in the league. Real Madrid enjoy significant advantage over Barcelona Barcelona are the second least-fouled team in La Liga, behind only Real Sociedad, who have received 113 free-kicks. Barcelona ahve conceded the second-fewest number of fouls in La Liga this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Despite dominating possession and frequently attempting to progress through opposition pressure, the Catalans have not received the same number of referee decisions in their favour as Real Madrid. As for Los Blancos, Mourinho’s team occupy the opposite end of the comparison. Their 171 fouls received are the highest in the division, while their 102 committed are the fewest. Furthermore, the individual statistics reinforce the contrast, as Fermin Lopez has committed 16 fouls, while Lamine Yamal, who has won 20 fouls, and Xavi Espart have registered 13 each. Conversely, Jude Bellingham leads the league for fouls won with 31. Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr. have 23 apiece, while Arda Guler has drawn 21. The El Clasico example Cucurella was never penalised for his challenges on Lamine Yamal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The October 25 meeting at Spotify Camp Nou, which Barcelona lost 1-2, offered a particularly relevant illustration. Marc Cucurella repeatedly challenged Lamine Yamal, with several incidents generating frustration among Barcelona fans. Several supporters highlighted the defender’s aggressive approach towards the young winger, while football pundits also questioned the decision not to award a free-kick when Yamal went down under Cucurella’s pressure late in the match. Now, there will be a debate regarding the matter, but the aforementioned statistics certainly bring forward a key question: if Real Madrid are indeed winning more fouls than any other team, why do they criticise La Liga officials? More importantly, is their campaign against referees influencing these statistics? If so, where is the transparency?

sports.title: Clough's longevity: landmark achievement or indictment on football?
sports.description: Nigel Clough took charge of Mansfield Town in November 2020 [Shutterstock] Becoming the longest-serving manager at a club takes some doing in the fickle world of football. Sticking around at two clubs long enough to hold that mantle is just about unprecedented. But Mansfield Town's Nigel Clough is about to redefine longevity as a manager when it comes to working at sides that make up the top 92 in the English pyramid. "I don't think it's particularly an achievement; I think it's more an indictment of football that nobody else has lasted that long," Clough told BBC Sport. This weekend he becomes the longest-serving manager – in terms of active years in the job and league matches at the helm – of the Stags, where he surpasses club great Ian Greaves. The 16 years Clough spent at Burton Albion, which took in around 900 matches across two spells spanning more than two decades, means the record at the east Staffordshire side is already his. Former England forward Clough is now six years and one week into the Stags job and is the second longest-serving manager across England's top four leagues - behind only Mikel Arteta at Arsenal - but he does not see his staying power as anything special. "I don't really think about it that much, I have to say. I'm just trying to get through the week," said Clough, who has been in charge of Mansfield for 329 matches across all competitions. When time pays dividends While Clough's players, as well as Mansfield fans have a different take on what his lengthy tenure at the One Call Stadium has meant, the 60-year-old reeled off the names of legendary past managers - his late father and iconic Nottingham Forest boss Brian Clough included - when reflecting on what joy clubs would have by sticking by their manager. "When you look back 20 or 30 years, my dad was at Forest for 18 years, Alex Ferguson was at Manchester United for so long and then there was Arsene Wenger at Arsenal. That was at the top level, but even lower down there was a lot of managers who stayed a lot of years," he said "I just think it's sad the way football is going at the moment. The first bad period that people have, a month, two months or something like that, and the manager is the one that goes." Clough, who played in the top flight for Forest, Liverpool and Manchester City, has been in management for 28 years and been in charge of just four clubs - Mansfield, Burton, Derby County and Sheffield United - in that time. Since bounding from non-league level - where he spent the first 10 years of his management career in his first spell at Burton - to take the reins of Derby in the Championship in 2009, no-one has overseen more matches than Clough's 893 across England's top four divisions. sports.title: Negreira case investigation effectively closed as Real Madrid await crucial Barcelona financial documents
sports.description: Negreira case investigation effectively closed as Real Madrid await crucial Barcelona financial documents The Negreira case remains one of the biggest controversies rocking Spanish football at the moment. Real Madrid continue to push for answers over Barcelona’s financial relationship with the former vice-president of the Spanish refereeing committee. Now, according to Que T’hi Jugues , the judicial committee has officially concluded its witness hearings. Only certain financial documents from Barcelona remain outstanding before a decision can be made on whether the case proceeds to trial. Former Barcelona officials defend usefulness of referee reports Former Barcelona B manager Gerard Lopez and ex-delegate Toni Alonso were the final witnesses to testify before investigating judge Alejandra Gil on Friday. Both defended the usefulness of the refereeing reports prepared by Javier Enriquez, son of former refereeing official Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira. Lopez coached Barcelona’s reserves between 2015 and 2018 and explained how reports on refereeing tendencies helped, especially in the lower divisions. Luis Enrique denied knowing of the technical reports that are at the centre of the Negreira case. (Photo by JAVIER SORIANO / AFP) (Photo by JAVIER SORIANO/AFP via Getty Images) Their testimony, however, contrasts with that of former first-team managers such as Luis Enrique and Ernesto Valverde. The two managers claimed that they were unaware of the reports or had never used them in any capacity during their time at the club. Barcelona continue to maintain that the payments were exclusively for technical consultancy services and not an attempt to influence refereeing decisions. Real Madrid await final documents before crucial judicial decision Real Madrid had requested a six-month extension to the investigation, alongside the prosecution, but the judge rejected the request in September. Nevertheless, Los Blancos successfully secured a partial ruling from the Barcelona Provincial Court requiring Barcelona to submit financial audits and reports covering 2010 to 2021. These are the documents still outstanding from the Catalan club before the investigation officially concludes. Real Madrid are closely following the proceedings of the Negreira case. (Photo by Dan Mullan/Getty Images) Once the documents are received, Judge Gil is expected to decide, potentially in early 2027, whether to dismiss the proceedings or send the case to trial. The investigation concerns payments reportedly totalling €8.4 million over 17 years to Negreira and related companies. Real Madrid are closely following the proceedings because, should Barcelona be found guilty, no other club would have been more affected than them. It remains to be seen how Judge Gil assesses the findings of this investigation and whether the case goes to trial in 2027.

sports.title: “She’s so good on the ball”: Eva Olid lavishes praise on surprise player ahead of Crystal Palace match
sports.description: “She’s so good on the ball”: Eva Olid lavishes praise on surprise player ahead of Crystal Palace match Manchester United Women manager Eva Olid has been speaking to the media ahead of her side’s home match in the Women’s Super League (WSL) against Crystal Palace. Squad updates Olid admitted she was still waiting for physio reports, but the only player definitely out is Scarlett Hill , who will be out of action for weeks. Hanna Lundkvist form The Catalan coach praised her side’s tactical performance versus Aston Villa last weekend and singled out the Swedish international Lundkvist for special praise. Olid explained, “I think she’s a player who can play in different positions. She can play as a full-back, a wing-back or a wide centre-back. With the national team, she’s also playing as a number six.” She continued, “she’s so good on the ball. She’s a player who can come inside and can play out wide. As a manager, you always like having those kinds of players because you know they’re versatile and can play in different positions, giving different things to the team.” Crystal Palace threat Explaining the type of threat Palace will pose, she asserted, “I expect a very competitive match. They’ve been having good matches, especially their last result against Tottenham on Wednesday. It was a very competitive match, and they could have won the game.” Olid continued, “for that reason, I expect a really good match, tactically and in terms of intensity. But, reluctantly, they made the trip, with Dearns' mother Tanya, a former New Zealand netballer, giving up her own coaching job to help the family settle in Japan. sports.description: Millie Bright said she wanted girls to feel "comfortable and confident" in their kit [BBC/Sally Hurst] Former England captain Millie Bright has helped hand out new kit to grassroots football teams in Leeds as part of an initiative aimed at keeping girls in sport for longer. Thirty teams based in communities facing social or economic challenges were chosen by anti-discrimination charity Kick it Out for the donation. Bright, who began her career at Doncaster Belles, said it was "vital" to keep girls playing sport. "Every young girl deserves a kit, no matter what level they play at, and, whilst the top of the game is doing really well, real life still exists. People can't afford to give their children kits, but that doesn't mean they should go without." Craig Gilmore set up Champions CIC, in Beeston, six years ago, to provide free Saturday morning training for children in the local area, as well as breakfast and lunch. "With the cost of living, football's expensive [and] bills come first," he said. "We work with a lot of families that can't afford the direct debits and the ongoing costs of grassroots sport nowadays. "The new kit is amazing. It gives them that sense of belonging, that team pride, it's a massive boost for them." Bright spoke with young footballers during the event in Leeds [BBC/Sally Hurst] The new kit was provided by Kick it Out, in partnership with the Morrisons Foundation. They hope it will inspire these girls to continue sport as young women and adults. "Girls' participation struggles with drop-out rates," said Gemma Clark, from Kick it Out. "One of the barriers is kit. We want to remove that barrier so that more local girls can keep playing." Bright told the BBC she was fully behind the campaign. "As a girl or a woman, it's about feeling wanted and equal," she said. "We deserve to have kits. I don't want to see any girl dropping out of the game because they don't feel valued or comfortable. "These are the days that really make a difference. Hopefully this shows the girls that the people at the top care. The power of having a kit is a small gesture, but has a massive impact." technology.description: Technology companies are doing just enough to show a degree of compliance with the UK's Online Safety Act, but are failing to meet the needs of the individuals and young victims the legislation exists to protect, experts say. A panel of online safety pros assembled before Parliament's Communications and Digital Committee on Tuesday, taking aim at the likes of Google, Microsoft, Meta, and ByteDance for failing to act on important matters. Clare McGlynn, professor of law at Durham University and expert on violence against women and girls (VAWG), was especially critical of major search engine providers for their inconsistent downranking of harmful content search terms. "Rape porn," for example, is correctly downranked and no user sees any relevant links until the tenth page of results, although adjacent terms such as "unwilling porn" can be found as early as the third page, McGlynn said. "I just think if someone spent a little more time thinking 'I really want to minimize the risk of this material appearing,' I would take a systematic approach," she told the committee. "I would downrank 'unwilling' and 'unwanted,' and I would downrank 'asleep porn' as well… because it just means that it's easily findable. "So, they don't rank some of them, but just not systematically or wholly consistently." McGlynn went on to say that during her own research, "force porn" was rightly downranked heavily, although terms as similar as "forced porn" were not. "If you were trying to think of the words that would be similar to say rape, and rape porn is extreme porn and it's not supposed to be on those platforms anymore, you would think of words like unwilling and unwanted," she added. "And we know your algorithm would." Google inevitably took much of McGlynn's flak due to its dominance of the search engine market, although the professor said the same issues can be observed on Bing, too. Alexandra Whiston-Dew, partner at law firm Miscon de Raya, argued that search engines have such an important role in regulating the OSA, noting the limited resources at Ofcom's disposal. She said that more needs to be done from the tech side to ensure different parties in the chain of publication are detected early and downranked or blocked accordingly. There are publications, for example, that actively advertise themselves as websites that host illegal content, and these appear to be missing from the search engines' crosshairs. technology.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
technology.description: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. Fifty-eight percent of adults 14­–39 years old who modified their use cited cost as a barrier, compared with just 20 percent of adults 65 or older who said the same. Read full article Comments

technology.description: Chalk up a new record for vulns. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. About 1.4 percent (1,363) of the CVEs published this year have been added to VulnCheck’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. “But obviously, as the number of CVEs grows, [1 percent] of 1,000 is a lot different than [1 percent] of 100,000,” Bressers said. Plus, as other security researchers have documented, the window between the public release of a security patch and attackers developing working exploits – often by reverse engineering the patch while end users are still applying the fix – is rapidly shrinking. technology.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
technology.description: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006).
